pairs.difference: A: a dead mid-gray ground mound fills the bottom third under a teal stripe wall. The navy tube and brown legs add little, so the card is almost entirely cool (warm_share 0.133, below the real floor of 0.239) with only 2.66 hue families. The ground has no local color. B: the honey plank floor carries amber-to-orange variation, and the green body and blue lenses sit against it as clear hue roles. B's shadows do go a dull olive-black (0.425, slightly low), but the palette reads as chosen.
pairs.fix: Replace the flat gray mound with ground that has a real local color, such as warm sandy beige with soft tan and lilac variation. Let some warm wood and brass color reflect into it so the card is not all cold teal and gray.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is near-pure red (subject chroma 0.2165, above the real ceiling), but its folds stay a rich deep red, as real shadows do, and the single gold badge is a clear accent. B: the rock is a muted mauve-brown whose lower half falls to a gray-brown mass (shadow kept 0.531, below the real 0.741 floor; subject 0.081, at the floor). The orange flame barely warms the rock next to it. Both cards break a range, so this is a weak call: B's chroma drop in shadow is further from the lessons than A's loud red.
pairs.fix: Keep color in the rock's shadow side: deep plum and warm red-brown, not gray-brown. Add orange light from the flame across the rock's rear edge and craters.

pairs.difference: A: flat azure sky, orange-tan sand, pure red stripe and royal blue base, all simple primaries. The shadow side keeps far more chroma than the lit side (2.04, above the real 1.435 ceiling) because the base's saturated blue dominates the shadow mass. The dish white is a good cool neutral, the one thing arguing against this call. B: peach sand castle against teal sea and a green bucket accent, with 6.04 hue families in range and shadows staying related terracotta. B's sand variation looks more natural.
pairs.fix: Soften the base from pure royal blue to a slightly dusty navy with gray-blue wear. Vary the sky and sand with gentle hue shifts, and make the red stripe a little less pure.

pairs.difference: A: lime sunburst against a lilac-gray ground, with a violet-blue pool of shadow under the rover. The orange body falls to dull brick in the lens, and white and gray dominate. Subject chroma 0.0576, warm_share 0.108, hue families 2.29 and shadow kept 0.298 are all below real ranges. Ground and hero share no color relationship, and the blue shadow looks painted on. B: the taxi's yellow stays a rich local yellow, deepening to amber, on a blue sunburst. Asphalt and shadow are warm dark browns, with 5.64 hue families.
pairs.fix: Make the rover's body a rich painted orange that stays saturated into its shadows. Change the gray ground to warm dusty tan and make the shadow under the vehicle a dark warm brown, not bright violet-blue.

pairs.difference: B: the whole card is magenta and pink, and the helmet white takes the same pink cast (warm_share 0.928 above the real ceiling, hue families 2.23 below the floor). The amber visor is the only other color. The lens shows the white shell and floor merging as pink-on-pink, with no neutral to rest the eye. A: blue shoes with green and pink trim on orange and cream, with neutral midsoles reading gray-tan. It is busy (5.49 hue families, above the 4.777 ceiling) but its colors stay separate.
pairs.fix: Keep the helmet shell a clean neutral white with cool gray-blue shadows, not pink. Shift the floor to a calmer, less pink tone so the helmet separates from it.

pairs.difference: A: pink, yellow and blue rings on green grass, with a warm brown fence behind. Loud, but the masses hold their local colors and the grass shadows stay rich (1.096). B: tan jacket with orange trim and green sash on a green burst, a restrained scheme with a low 2.53 hue families but a related brown shadow. Background chroma is only marginally over on each card, so nothing here points either way.

B: a violet night sky over a lilac-gray ground, with pinkish-beige light and periwinkle shadow on the ground. The dome frame is cream with warm white, a recognisable generated cream shift. The door's yellow is the only warm accent. Hue families 3.0 are just below the floor, and the ground has no local color. A: pool, thatch, fruit and green stools hold distinct local colors, shadows go to deep brown and teal, and the only flag is many hue families (7.05, over the 6.448 ceiling).
pairs.fix: Give the ground a believable local color, such as pale cool dust with subtle blue-gray and tan. Make the trim a neutral white with soft blue-gray shadow, not cream, and drop the pink glow on the ground.

pairs.difference: A: the orange-and-cream planet and yellow ring sit on purple with a pale pink-white halo round the planet, the same glow the generated lesson cards use. The lens shows the planet with almost no separate shadow hue, only peach and cream masses. The hero's dark side stays orange rather than shifting. B: coral flip-flops with golden straps on aqua, with shadows stepping to a related deeper red-orange. Both are in range on the numbers, so this rests on the halo and missing shadow hue.
pairs.fix: Remove the white-pink glow around the planet. Let its shadow side turn to a deep red-brown with a hint of purple from the background.

pairs.difference: A: cream pages, warm wood and a red book cover, with green foliage for relief. Shadows stay rich brown-orange, and the whole card is warm (0.758). B: green seat on a red-coral wall and peach floor, with the gray frame picking up red. It is also warm (0.876). Both exceed the warm ceiling in the same way, and each has clear hue roles and related shadows, so color does not separate them.

A: orange player on violet rings, the body one flat orange mass in the lens, cool lilac-white earbuds, background chroma 0.2384 over the ceiling and 1.81 hue families under the floor. B: neutral steel saucer with lime dome and orange lights on yellow rings, the metal picking up yellow reflections, warm_share 0.848 over the ceiling. Each card breaks a different range and neither shows the cream or orange shift from the lessons.

B: teal console on flat orange with a mid-gray floor. The floor has no local color and no bounce from the orange wall, and it reads as a separate plate. Subject chroma 0.0698 and hue families 2.64 are both just under the floors. In the lens, the red and yellow buttons collapse into one orange. A: red, gold and blue with pale pink-cream paving, shadows go to deep maroon and brown, and whites keep a slightly cool edge. Hue roles are clear and all values are in range.
pairs.fix: Tint the floor with warm orange bounce and a soft local color instead of plain mid-gray. Keep red and yellow buttons clearly different hues, and let the console's shadows go to deep blue-green.

pairs.difference: A: silver-blue rocket with red fins on cyan, the metal keeping a clean cool neutral. B: yellow submarine with copper trim on deep green with a center glow, yellow stepping to amber-brown in shadow, background chroma 0.0948 slightly under the floor. Hue roles are clear on both, and shadows stay rich. The small background shortfall on B is not a finding on its own.

pattern: Generated cards are given away by missing local color in the neutrals and in the shadow hue, not by raw loudness. Three things recur. Ground planes are a plain mid or lilac gray that shares no color with the hero or backdrop (p01 A, p04 A, p07 B, p11 B). Whites drift to cream or take on the backdrop's cast instead of staying neutral with cool shadows (p05 B, p07 B, and the lesson monitors). Halos glow around the hero, and its shadow side stays the same hue instead of shifting (p08 A, and the lesson gloves). Real cards pair saturated backdrops with believable local materials and with shadows that move to a related dark hue. The reading stayed on color alone; subject matter was not used, and p02, p03 and the three 'neither' calls at 2 are weak.
